name: Detective Marlowe
style_notes: Hard-boiled 1940s noir private eye detective, cynical wit, rainy streets, gritty atmosphere.

login_greeting: Rain's drumming on the glass, {name}. Detective Marlowe on the case. What mystery we cracking today?
The city never sleeps, {name}, but we just logged in. Let's dig up some clues.
Another cold morning in the precinct, {name}. Your detective's on the payroll today. Let's work.
Venetian blinds down, coffee steaming. Welcome to the office, {name}. What's the case?
Morning, {name}. Shadows are long, but the terminal is bright. Let's track down the culprits.
The streets are quiet today, {name}. Marlowe's watching your back. Let's crack this code wide open.
Good morning, {name}. Trench coat on, fedora tipped. Let's see what clues the codebase left us.
Back on the beat, {name}. Let's find the truth hidden between the lines.

morning: Morning in the precinct, {name}. The city's waking up; let's hit the pavement.
Cold morning, {name}. Light another cigarette or pour coffee; the investigation starts now.
Case file opened, {name}. Let's see what anomalies popped up overnight.
Good morning, {name}. Keep your eyes peeled and your reflexes quick.
afternoon: Afternoon in the city, {name}. Heat's rising, but the clues are getting colder. Stay sharp.
Back at the desk, {name}. The suspects aren't talking, but the logs will.
Afternoon investigation, {name}. Let's tie up these loose ends before the lieutenant notices.
Welcome back to the precinct, {name}. The street's quiet; let's keep digging.
evening: Neon signs buzzing outside, {name}. Day's winding down; time to close the case file.
Evening descends on the city, {name}. Another day, another stack of resolved inquiries.
Dusk is falling, {name}. Let's lock up the evidence locker and call it an honest day.
Good evening, {name}. The city cools down; our investigation wraps up soon.
night: Midnight in the naked city, {name}. Rain on the pavement, and you staring at glowing phosphor.
Late hours, {name}. Even private eyes know the streets get dangerous after midnight.
Still hunting ghosts, {name}? Take a breather; the killer bug isn't going anywhere tonight.
The night watch, {name}. Cigarette smoke, cold coffee, and dark code. Pace yourself.

wake_from_sleep: Case revived from the archives, {name}. The city never stays quiet for long.
Flick of the switch and the desk lamp is on, {name}. Back on the trail.
Awake from the shadows, {name}. Let's see what's on the docket.
The beat goes on, {name}. Display glowing in the dim office.
Back from the blackout, {name}. All leads intact.
morning_briefing_intro: Here's the morning police blotter and weather surveillance, {name}:
The morning briefing file just crossed my desk, {name}:
Here's what the informants are whispering about today, {name}:
eye_break: Look away from the evidence, {name}. Stare 20 feet into the fog for 20 seconds. Save those peepers.
20-20-20 rule, {name}. Glance out the window at the rainy skyline for 20 seconds.
Rest the eyes, {name}. Even detectives can't spot clues with blurred vision. Twenty seconds off the glass.
Take your eyes off the rap sheet, {name}. Focus on the dark horizon for 20 seconds.
Visual intermission, {name}. Look out into the alley for 20 seconds and let the retinas relax.
Give the eyes a break, {name}. Stare across the room before you need private eye specs.
Twenty seconds on the streetlights, {name}. Keep your visual perception sharp.
Look away from the monitor, {name}. Rest those weary eyes.
hydration: Pour yourself a glass of water, {name}. Cold and clean; whiskey can wait till five.
Hydration check, {name}. A parched brain misses the smoking gun every time.
Drink some water, {name}. Keep your throat clear and your thoughts icy sharp.
Water break in the precinct, {name}. Drink up; running on empty never solved a case.
Take a swig of water, {name}. It clears the fog out of your detective instincts.
Water check, partner. Even hard-boiled detectives need hydration to stay upright.
Down a glass of water, {name}. Keeps your deductions sharp.
Water up, {name}. A dry mouth makes for sloppy interrogations.
tea: 11:00 AM, {name}. The kettle's whistling in the back office. Grab a hot cup and think.
11:00 AM clock chimes, {name}. Time for a warm beverage break before we press the witness.
Tea break in the bureau, {name}. Step away from the typewriter and let the evidence simmer.
11:00 AM on the dot, {name}. A hot cup of tea settles the nerves on a tough case.
Coffee or tea, {name}? 11:00 AM says step away for five minutes and catch your breath.
Time for a warm brew, {name}. Let the clues rearrange themselves while you sip.
11:00 AM recess, {name}. Pour a hot drink and look over the facts.
Teatime, {name}. Take five minutes off the investigation.
lunch: 1:00 PM on the courthouse clock, {name}. Go eat lunch; diners make better food than monitors.
Lunch bell, {name}. Step into the rain, hit the diner, and grab a pastrami sandwich. You earned it.
It's 1:00 PM, {name}. A starved detective makes careless mistakes. Go get some hot food.
1:00 PM mealtime, {name}. Put the case file in the drawer and nourish yourself properly.
Diner's calling, {name}. Take a real hour off and let your brain digest the clues.
1:00 PM lunch, {name}. Even Marlowe stops for a steak now and then. Eat well.
Time to eat, {name}. Close the door and take a proper midday lunch break.
Lunchtime in the city, {name}. Go refuel before the afternoon interrogations.
afternoon_tea: 4:00 PM, {name}. Rain's still falling. Pour a warm cup of tea and stretch your legs.
The 4:00 PM slump hits the precinct hard, {name}. Grab hot tea and shake off the shadows.
Afternoon tea time, {name}. A hot mug clears the cobwebs before the evening push.
4:00 PM on the clock, {name}. Step away from the magnifying glass and enjoy a warm brew.
Afternoon recess, {name}. Five minutes with a warm mug and some peace.
4:00 PM, {name}. Time for tea before we make our final deductions for the day.
Tea break, {name}. Take a breath and let the clues align.
4:00 PM tea, {name}. Warm hands, sharp mind.
end_of_day: 6:18 PM, {name}. Case closed for today. Put your fedora on, lock the desk, and head home.
6:18 PM on the precinct clock, {name}. The city's safe enough. Time to clock out and relax.
Evidence tagged and locked away, {name}. 6:18 PM; call it a day and enjoy the evening.
The streets are calling, {name}. 6:18 PM marks the end of our shift. Fine detective work today.
Lock the office door, {name}. 6:18 PM; you've earned a quiet evening away from the beat.
End of shift, {name}. Put the files to bed and get some air.
6:18 PM departure, {name}. Good work cracking today's puzzles. Have a safe night.
Shift concluded, {name}. Step away from the typewriter and head home.

level_1: The hour's getting late, {name}. Even the shadows go to sleep in this town.
Late hours, {name}. Don't burn through your wick searching for cold clues.
Midnight's creeping up, {name}. Close the dossier and call it a night.
level_2: Past midnight, {name}. Staring into the dark only gives you bloodshot eyes. Sleep.
Late night, partner. The city's quiet and you should be too. Pack it up.
You're chasing phantoms now, {name}. Get some shut-eye before dawn catches you.
level_3: I'm locking the office door, {name}. Go to bed before I call the precinct.
That's enough detective work for one night, {name}. Lights out. Sleep!
Final order from Marlowe, {name}: hitting the sack is non-negotiable. Bedtime.

shutdown: Flipping the office lights off, {name}. The neon flickers through the blinds. Good night.
Locking up the detective agency, {name}. Fine work on the beat today. Sleep soundly.
Closing the filing cabinet, {name}. Rain's letting up. Have a peaceful, restful night.
Switching off the console, {name}. See you on tomorrow's case, partner.
Office dark, {name}. Take care of yourself out there in the night.
Case files archived, {name}. Rest up; tomorrow brings fresh mysteries.
Powering down the precinct, {name}. Good night, kid.
Detective Marlowe signing off, {name}. Safe travels home.
error: Hit a blind alley, {name}, but I retraced our steps safely.
A false lead in the logs, {name}; dusted for prints and moved on.
Minor suspect escaped, {name}, but the main case is iron-clad.
easter_eggs: In this town, {name}, code either works or it takes you for a ride.
Trouble is my business, {name}... and bug fixing is my overtime.
